business.description: Valiant Laboratories Limited is a pharmaceutical company and one of India's leading manufacturers of high-quality Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), with a strong presence in the Paracetamol API segment. The company has over 45 years of manufacturing excellence and is part of the Aarti Group of Industries.

outlook.statement: Targeting WHO-GMP compliance by next year to support entry into semi-regulated export markets
Focus on accelerating commercialization of products from VASPL development pipeline while expanding export footprint across key international markets
Priorities for FY27: consolidate deleveraged balance sheet, support VASPL's commercial ramp-up, and continue aligning facilities with international regulatory requirements

The Indian economy is expected to moderate from the exceptional pace of FY 2025-26 while remaining among the fastest-growing major economies. Real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 projected at 6.6% by RBI (down from 6.9%), 6.4% by IMF, and 6.8%-7.2% range by Economic Survey 2025-26.
Global pharmaceutical market projected to increase from approximately US$ 1,881.67 billion in 2026 to US$ 3,219.76 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 6.15% during the forecast period.
Global API market projected to grow from approximately US$ 256.4 billion in 2025 to US$ 376.2 billion by 2034, registering a CAGR of 4.22% during 2026-2034.

Indian API industry projected to grow at a CAGR of 5% to 7% in FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28, driven by favourable government policy, structural shift towards high-potency and complex APIs, rising domestic demand and deeper penetration of regulated and emerging markets.

Demand for Paracetamol in India expected to grow broadly in line with wider analgesic and antipyretic segment over medium term, supported by sustained healthcare demand, expanding pharmaceutical access and increasing penetration of organised retail and digital pharmacy networks. Growth is volume-led rather than price-led.

RBI raised CPI inflation projection for FY 2026-27 by 50 basis points to 5.1%, with quarterly profile of 4.2% in Q1, 5.1% in Q2, 5.9% in Q3 and 5.4% in Q4, and core inflation at 4.7%. For a manufacturer dependent on power, steam, solvents and freight, this points to a higher input-cost environment in FY 2026-27 than in the year under review.

US Section 232 proclamation imposing additional ad valorem duty of up to 100% on patented pharmaceutical products and associated APIs/KSMs takes effect from 31 July 2026 (larger companies) and 29 September 2026 (smaller manufacturers). Generic pharmaceuticals, biosimilars and associated ingredients expressly excluded; Paracetamol falls outside scope at present. However, Secretary of Commerce to advise within one year (by ~April 2027) whether tariffs should be extended to generic pharmaceuticals and their ingredients - a genuine forward risk for Indian API industry.

Actual results could differ from those expressed or implied. Important factors that could make a difference to the Company's operations include economic conditions affecting demand-supply and price conditions in the domestic and overseas markets in which the Company operates, changes in the government regulations, tax laws and other statutes and other incidental factors.

The Board of Directors approved the evaluation of potential restructuring options involving the Company, its holding company, subsidiaries and associates, with a view to achieving operational efficiencies, organizational alignment and strategic synergies. As on the date of this Report, no definitive decision has been taken and the evaluation process remains ongoing.

Focus for FY27 is to accelerate the commercialization of products from VASPL development pipeline while expanding export footprint across key international markets; consolidate deleveraged balance sheet, support VASPL's commercial ramp-up, and continue aligning facilities with international regulatory requirements; targeting WHO-GMP compliance by next year to support entry into semi-regulated export markets

The principal near-term driver of consolidated profitability is raising throughput at the capacity commissioned during FY 2025-26. Management's focus is on stabilising the process, completing customer validations and progressively increasing plant utilisation.

Through Valiant Advanced Sciences Private Limited, the Company is developing specialty chemicals where products will find end-use applications in the agrochemical, pharmaceutical, dye, pigment, fragrance, food, and polymer industries.

Continued investment in process improvement, solvent recovery, energy efficiency and yield enhancement is intended to protect margins in a market where selling prices are largely externally determined.

As global pharmaceutical and chemical supply chains continue to diversify, Indian manufacturers are gaining greater opportunities to expand their international footprint. Supported by manufacturing expertise, quality standards and cost competitiveness, the Company is well positioned to leverage emerging export opportunities and strengthen its presence in global markets.

CareEdge Ratings projects that the Indian API industry will grow at a compound annual growth rate of 5% to 7% in FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28, driven by favourable government policy, a structural shift towards high-potency and complex APIs, rising domestic demand and deeper penetration of regulated and emerging markets.
The global API market is projected to grow from approximately US$ 256.4 billion in 2025 to US$ 376.2 billion by 2034, registering a CAGR of 4.22% during 2026-2034.
The global pharmaceutical industry is projected to increase from approximately US$ 1,881.67 billion in 2026 to US$ 3,219.76 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 6.15% during the forecast period.
The Indian chemical industry is projected to reach approximately US$ 230-255 billion by 2030, registering a CAGR of 8-9% over the next five to six years.

Independent estimates place the Indian specialty chemicals market at approximately US$ 63 billion to US$ 67 billion in 2024-25, growing at between 6% and 9% a year to approximately US$ 89 billion to US$ 95 billion by 2030.
The Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India projects that the industry will reach approximately US$ 130 billion by 2030, implying a compound annual growth rate in excess of 10%.

Demand for Paracetamol in India is expected to grow broadly in line with the wider analgesic and antipyretic segment over the medium term, supported by sustained healthcare demand, expanding pharmaceutical access and increasing penetration of organised retail and digital pharmacy networks.

The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on May 16, 2026, approved the evaluation of potential restructuring options involving the Company, its holding company, subsidiaries and associates, with a view to achieving operational efficiencies, organizational alignment and strategic synergies. As on the date of this Report, no definitive decision has been taken and the evaluation process remains ongoing.

other_notable: Rights Issue completed in August 2025 raised Rs 81.47 crore, majority used to fully repay outstanding term borrowings
Revenue from operations grew 62.7% to Rs 217.04 crore in FY26
Returned to profitability with PAT of Rs 5.55 crore in FY26 vs loss of Rs 2.15 crore in FY25
EBITDA margin recovered to 4.64% from 0.56% in FY25
Zero Lost Time Injuries, zero Medical Treatment Cases, zero occupational illnesses and no fatal accidents in FY26
Planted 50+ trees at facility and initiated Miyawaki-style green belt development
Installed Mechanical Vapour Recompression (MVR) system with Reverse Osmosis (RO) plant achieving Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD)
Transitioned to LED lighting and installed energy meters at departmental and equipment levels
Rights Issue of 1,08,62,500 equity shares at Rs 75 per share (face value Rs 10 and securities premium Rs 65), allotted on 11 August 2025, raised Rs 81.47 crore
Consolidated capital work-in-progress of Rs 155.78 crore as at 31 March 2025 substantially capitalised during the year, with Rs 168.57 crore transferred from CWIP into property, plant and equipment
Consolidated gross block rose from Rs 69.01 crore to Rs 252.61 crore
Asset turnover (revenue from operations to average capital employed) remains low at approximately 0.69 times; principal metric management will seek to improve in FY 2026-27
Consolidated inventories increased from Rs 3.99 crore to Rs 45.43 crore, principally raw material secured to support ramp-up of expanded capacity
Trade payables increased from Rs 40.72 crore to Rs 94.02 crore

Trade receivables grew 29.73% against revenue growth of 78.04%, representing improvement in collection efficiency; receivable days remain elevated at approximately 127 days of consolidated revenue from operations
Customer concentration reduced: top 3 customers accounted for 16.76% of standalone revenue from operations (vs 17.19% in FY 2024-25); top 5 customers for 23.43% (vs 25.22%)

Production Linked Incentive Scheme for bulk drugs carries outlay of Rs 6,940 crore; Bulk Drug Parks scheme outlay of Rs 3,000 crore; more than 30 projects completed and commissioned, nearly 80% of ongoing API investment projects linked to bulk drug parks initiative
Para-amino phenol (key starting material for Paracetamol) on list of key starting materials eligible for support under PLI scheme
Anti-dumping duty on Paracetamol imports from China (most recently at US$ 787 per tonne) terminated in 2019; domestic manufacturers compete directly with imported material on price
India's chemical industry estimated at US$ 155-165 billion, projected to reach US$ 230-255 billion by 2030 (CAGR 8-9%)
Indian specialty chemicals market estimated at US$ 63-67 billion in 2024-25, growing at 6-9% annually to US$ 89-95 billion by 2030
India's chemicals trade deficit estimated at US$ 31 billion in 2025, concentrated in inorganic chemicals (~US$ 12 billion) and polymers (~US$ 13 billion)

The Company was originally formed as a partnership firm under Indian Partnership Act, 1932, under the name and style of 'M/s. Bharat Chemicals'. Subsequently, the partnership firm, M/s. Bharat Chemicals was converted into a public limited company under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, with the name 'Valiant Laboratories Limited' pursuant to certificate of incorporation dated August 16, 2021.

On October 06, 2023, the Company successfully completed the IPO process, and the equity shares of the Company are listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and the BSE Limited (BSE).
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on July 09, 2025, approved the offer and issuance of equity shares by way of a Rights Issue for an amount not exceeding H 8,146.88 Lakhs.

The Rights Issue shares were offered in the ratio of 1 (one) Rights Equity Share for every 4 (four) fully paid-up equity shares held by eligible shareholders as on the record date, i.e., July 19, 2025.
The Rights Issue opened on July 28, 2025, and closed on August 08, 2025.

Upon successful completion on August 13, 2025, the post-issue paid-up share capital of the Company stands increased to H 54,31,25,000/- (Rupees Fifty-Four Crore Thirty-One Lakh Twenty-Five Thousand Only), comprising 5,43,12,500 Equity Shares of face value of H 10/- each.

The Company has been rated by India Ratings and Research vide its letter dated June 25, 2025, for the Company's banking facilities: Fund-based working capital limits H 550 million - IND BBB/Stable/IND A2; Non-fund-based working capital limits H 10 million - IND A2.
With a view to conserve resources for expansion of business, the Directors of the Company have considered it prudent not to recommend any dividend for the year under review.
During the year under review, the Company has not transferred any amount of profit to the reserves.
The Company has not accepted any deposits within the meaning of Sections 73 of the Act.
The Company has received the requisite declarations from Ms. Sonal Vira confirming that she meets the criteria of independence as prescribed under the Act and the Listing Regulations.

In terms of requirements of Schedule IV of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, 1 (One) meeting of the Independent Directors was held on February 11, 2026.

The Company has constituted various Board level committees: Audit Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Stakeholders' Relationship Committee, Risk Management Committee, Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, Rights Issue Committee (dissolved on November 11, 2025), Restructuring Committee (w.e.f. March 07, 2026).
As the Company does not fall under any of the threshold limits given under the provisions of Section 135 of the Act, the compliances under CSR are not applicable to the Company.
The Company is not ranked among the top 1000 listed entities for the FY 2025-26. Consequently, the company is not required to include the BRSR in the Annual Report for this period.
50+ trees were planted in the green belt and garden areas in and around the facility during the year, reinforcing the Company's commitment to long-term ecological balance.

The Occupational Health Centre maintained first-aid boxes and stretchers during the year, with personnels trained in first aid by an authorized first-aid trainer. Periodic health check-ups were conducted, first-aid facilities and health records were maintained and kept updated.
Zero Lost Time Injury (LTI) and Zero Medical Treatment Case (MTC) during the year, with no fatal accidents reported.
Near-miss incidents and unsafe acts/conditions proactively reported and tracked with corrective and preventive actions implemented.
Mock drills conducted including plant-wide emergency drill and dedicated mock drill on electric shock emergency response.
Safety Week celebrated with full participation from employees and contract workers.
Facility-wide cleaning drive carried out jointly by staff and contract workers.
Foreign Exchange Earnings: Rs 409.75 Lakhs; Foreign Exchange Outgo: Rs 5238.61 Lakhs.
No capital investment in energy conservation equipment during the year.
Expenditure incurred on Research and Development: NIL.
No application made or proceeding pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
No one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution.
No requirement of transferring any unpaid/unclaimed dividend to IEPF.
No instances of fraud reported by Statutory Auditors under Section 143(12) of the Act.

Secretarial Audit Report and Annual Secretarial Compliance Report for FY 2025-26 do not contain any qualification, reservation or adverse remark except for delay in prior intimation of Rights Issue Committee Meeting.
